reasoning: The two attempts are almost the same. They have the same model.json, file placement, handling of existing players, and pcall retry loop, and every check passes for both. A wins narrowly. It uses strict typing. Its server sets a StarterKitGiven marker after all the counts, which gives the client one reliable completion signal and also stops the kit from being given twice. B is also correct and arguably more conventional, because it uses an instance-path require and adds no extra attribute. But it is untyped and detects completion less directly. The gap is small.

criteria.criterion: StarterKit declared in mapped Rojo files
criteria.note: src/ReplicatedStorage/Shared/StarterKit.model.json has className Configuration and builds under ReplicatedStorage.Shared.
Brick 20, Dirt 20, Grass 10, Window 0, Wood 10 are all unquoted numbers.
StarterKit.server.luau is in ServerScriptService and StarterKitNotification.client.luau is in StarterPlayerScripts.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit correctly, covers every BlockTypes.List entry
criteria.note: Finds StarterKit with a recursive FindFirstChild plus an IsA assert, loops over BlockTypes.List, and gives 0 with a warning when a value is missing, NaN or negative.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, guarded SetCore
criteria.note: Loops over GetPlayers; the client waits for the StarterKitGiven attribute, which the server sets after every count, then calls SetCore inside pcall up to 20 times, 0.5 s apart.
Only the three kit files changed, and luau-lsp, selene, StyLua and rojo build all pass.

criteria.criterion: StarterKit declared in mapped Rojo files
criteria.note: Same StarterKit.model.json file under Shared, with className Configuration.
All five values are JSON numbers.

criteria.criterion: Reads StarterKit correctly, covers every BlockTypes.List entry
criteria.note: findConfig does a recursive find and checks the type; getStarterCount warns separately for a missing or non-number attribute, falls back to 0, and clamps with math.max.

criteria.criterion: Existing players, one-time notification, guarded SetCore
criteria.note: Uses task.spawn over GetPlayers; waitForCounts loops on AttributeChanged until every block count is a number, then calls SetCore through pcall with retries.
Only the kit files changed, and all checks pass.

strengths: Sets a StarterKitGiven attribute after the counts, so the client has one clear signal that the kit is complete
Guards against giving the kit twice and handles NaN and negative values
weaknesses: Adds an extra StarterKitGiven attribute to the Player that the task didn't ask for
Uses @game string requires, which depends on the project's require convention
The attribute name is duplicated in the server and client scripts (a comment says to keep them in sync)

strengths: Uses the standard instance-path require, which works for sure
Waits for every count rather than a separate marker attribute, so it adds no extra attributes
Doesn't overwrite counts that something else already set
Gives clear warnings for missing and non-number attributes
weaknesses: Not in strict mode, and relies on casts (config :: Configuration, count :: number)
The client's waitForCounts re-scans every block type on any attribute change, which is slightly less direct than a completion marker
The client requires through ReplicatedStorage.Shared without WaitForChild (usually fine)
